records.name: C.O.D.E. (Community of Developers & Engineers)
records.summary: A community for people who build software in Philadelphia. Members meet for weekly coding sessions to work on problems side by side, and the group runs a hackathon every quarter.
records.what_you_do: Bring a laptop, work on your own code or a challenge with others, and help newer members get unstuck. Some weeks focus on practice problems.

schedule.text: Weekly coding sessions. The group's page names LeetCode Wednesdays; check the Meetup calendar for times and locations.

cost.text: Not stated on the group's site; the site asks for donations and sponsors and lists no ticket price.

first_step.how: Join the group's Discord, RSVP on Meetup for the next session, and come with a laptop
first_step.basis: The group's own onboarding page gives three steps for new people and welcomes them to weekly sessions

records.notes: Meetup topic page lists this group as C.O.D.E. (Community of Developers & Engineers) under the slug code-coffee-philly; the group's own site is codephilly.com. Dated items on the group's site: AI Agent Hackathon build day September 20, 2026 and demo night September 22, 2026, both at Philadelphia venues. Found via Meetup topic page for software development (lead) and verified on the group's own site. Schedule times and location not confirmed on the group site. Credit: lead came from a Meetup topic page; no facts taken from Meetup.

records.name: Code for Philly
records.summary: Volunteers who build free, open source tools that help the public in Philadelphia. The group keeps a directory of projects where people can find a place to help.
records.what_you_do: Pick a civic project from the directory, contribute code or skills, and help start new projects.

schedule.text: The group holds a regular meetup and hackathons; dates are posted on Meetup and were not confirmed on its own site.

cost.text: Free to take part in volunteer projects, as far as the group's site describes

first_step.how: Browse the project directory on codeforphilly.org and read the Projects 101 guide for new volunteers
first_step.basis: The group's projects page points new volunteers to a Projects 101 guide and a getting started repository

records.notes: Lead from Meetup topic page for software development (listed as Code for Philly, slug code-for-philly). Fetches of the group's own pages returned only the page title, so facts above come from search summaries of codeforphilly.org, not a full read. No dated evidence found, so status is unknown. Needs a human or a re-fetch before publishing with confidence. Founded 2012 under Code for America's Brigade program, per search summary.

records.name: Philadelphia Red Hat User Group
records.summary: A local meetup for people who use Red Hat and open source tools. Members get together in person for talks and hands on sessions, and the group is run as part of Red Hat's user group program.
records.what_you_do: Attend the talks and sessions, meet other technical users, and learn how Red Hat tools are used in real work.

schedule.text: Sessions are scheduled as events; the next listed session is Tuesday, November 3, 2026, from 3 to 6 pm.

cost.text: Free to register, as shown on the Red Hat event listing

first_step.how: Register through the link on Red Hat's events listing for the next session, or check the group's Meetup page
first_step.basis: Sessions are open to the public and listed with a registration link, though the venue is not published on that listing

records.notes: The group has no website of its own; the facts come from Red Hat's public listing, which links to the Meetup group philadelphia-rhug. Red Hat's listing also showed a March 26, 2026 session. Venue not listed for the November session. Meetup lead came from the Meetup topic page for software development. The listing says to email rhug@redhat.com about starting a group, which is not recorded as a contact here. Schedule text and draft commitment should be double-checked against the Meetup page.

records.name: Philly AI Connect
records.summary: A Philadelphia community for people interested in artificial intelligence and machine learning. It runs talks, speaker sessions, workshops, and networking, and welcomes volunteers and speakers.
records.what_you_do: Attend talks and demos, join the group's Discord to work on open source projects, or sign up to volunteer or speak.

schedule.text: Events are held as talks and summits; the site lists past events through May 7, 2026 and no upcoming dates.

cost.text: Not stated on the group's site

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer sign up form on the group's site, or follow its Meetup page for the next event
first_step.basis: Events are open to the public, but the RSVP button on the site has no link, so the Meetup page is the way to sign up

records.notes: Lead from Meetup topic page for machine learning. Group site lists a May 7, 2026 summit and earlier talks back to 2023. Site lists no upcoming events on the day seen. Technical.ly's 2025 meetup guide also lists the group.

records.name: Philly Tech Entrepreneurs
records.summary: A free community for local tech founders, developers, designers, and students. Members chat on Slack, follow Meetup events, and meet in person around the Philadelphia area.
records.what_you_do: Introduce yourself in the Slack community, meet other founders and builders at events, and share what you are working on.

schedule.text: Events are held around Philadelphia; the group's site lists no regular meeting day or time.

cost.text: Membership is free; some events have a ticket of about $10, and each event page says whether it is free

first_step.how: Join the Slack community and introduce yourself, then join the Meetup group to follow events
first_step.basis: Membership is free and open to anyone who lives near enough to attend in person, with a clear way to join

records.notes: Lead from Technical.ly's 2025 Philadelphia meetup guide and the Meetup topic page for entrepreneurs. Newest dated item on the site is a February 2024 podcast emblem upload; footer reads 2024. No upcoming events listed, so status is dormant. Review before showing as a current group. Meetup and Slack links were not recorded because no direct invite links were confirmed.

records.name: DataPhilly (Data Science Philadelphia)
records.summary: A community of data science and analytics people in Philadelphia. It hosts talks, hands on workshops, and panel discussions on topics such as AI, big data, and statistical modeling, and welcomes beginners.
records.what_you_do: Attend talks and workshops, join the Meetup group for events, and connect with others working with data.

schedule.text: Events are listed on Meetup; the group's site does not state a regular day or time.

cost.text: Not stated on the group's site

first_step.how: Use the Join Us page on the group's site, then follow its Meetup group for events
first_step.basis: The site says it welcomes beginners and experts and links to a join page and a Meetup group

records.notes: Lead from the Meetup topic page for machine learning and Technical.ly's 2025 meetup guide. Group's own site shows a link to an October 2025 events page but no event details were readable, so the status is weak. Site footer reads 2025. Social link above is the general LinkedIn home page, not the group's page; replace with the group's LinkedIn page if it is confirmed.

notes: Platform use: 6 Meetup topic pages (software development, makers, women in tech, entrepreneurs, machine learning, public speaking). The makers, women in tech, entrepreneurs, machine learning and public speaking topic pages returned no group names, so Meetup was not a productive source this run; the Meetup topic pages that worked were software development only. Join Philly was not used. Credit: leads from Meetup topic pages and the Technical.ly guides. Technical.ly was used as a source for leads and as a non-platform source. Out of area or not Philadelphia: Microsoft Reactor New York (listed on the software development topic page, New York) and Newark Area Cohousing (Newark, not Philadelphia). Not recorded: Sports Business Leaders (sportsbusinessleaders.com) is a sports business networking organization, not a Philadelphia community program. Dropped: CARES caregiver support at Lutheran Settlement House (1340 Frankford Ave). Only a 2014 listing was found for its support group, and the homepage fetch showed no CARES page. Lutheran Settlement House phone 215-426-8610. Recommend a separate check of the Older Adults services page at lutheransettlement.org/lsh-services/senior-services/. Searches: 6 of 8 used; no searches left unused for a retry. Fetches used: about 26. Several group sites (Code for Philly) returned only page titles, so those records are low confidence.
